correctness.rationale: For a vertex in part \(i\), the closed-neighborhood intersection has size \(1+b-b_i\) if selected and \(b-b_i\) otherwise. If \(b\le k\) feasibility is automatic. If \(b>k\), every part must contain a selected vertex and the selected-vertex inequality is exactly \(b_i\ge b-k+1\); it is also sufficient. For a fixed size \(s>k\), feasibility is equivalent to \(s-k+1\le\min_i n_i\), \(r(s-k+1)\le s\), and \(s\le N\), which yields the maximum formula. Fresh literal replay checked 42,640 cases through order seven.

final_claim: For every connected complete multipartite graph and \(k\ge1\), a set of size at most \(k\) is automatically a \(k\)-limited packing, while a larger set of size \(b\) is feasible exactly when every part contributes at least \(b-k+1\) selected vertices; the stated all-size enumerator and closed formula for \(L_k(G)\) follow.
limitations: The theorem is for closed-neighborhood limited packing, not total/open-neighborhood variants.
